says: In today's CI, SC21's bare-github pattern matches the plain word GitHub in any text of the workflow, not only inside ${{ }} expressions, so a step name or run line such as 'Publish to GitHub' gets SC21's error that it reads the hand start's inputs.
proof: A scratch node script ran lintScheduled at c83fe39bc on the real scheduled.yaml with the report step's env set to one value at a time. It printed `other true Publish to GitHub`, `other true see github docs` and `other true uses GitHub's runner` (named by SC21), and `real: []` for the unchanged file.
cost: A misleading block the next time a step's name or script says GitHub. The fix is to scan only expressions (${{ }} and if values).
